newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures pare gains, NY takes breather.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures pare gains, NY takes breather.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures wandered in a tight range in the afternoon after a relatively quiet New York session and prices ended the day with pared gains.
The market had nudged higher at the start on short-covering buying but Indonesian origin offers knocked it back from the peaks.
It made little headway in the afternoon after New York arabica futures slowed its advance after Wednesday's rally to 2-1/2 year high in reaction to bullish U.S. stock data released late on Tuesday.
"New York is virtually at a standstill today, probably taking a breather from yesterday's rally," said one.
Benchmark May gave up further gains by the close, settling just $5 higher at $1,615 a tonne while July firmed $13 at $1,643.
May/July switches were again active as funds rolled forward their May positions.
European traders said the New York arabica futures remained vulnerable to further spike higher.
"There are two strikes coming up, the certified stocks are low and the May spread is widening," said one. "A few roasters are not covered and I think May could continue to rise."
Traders' nerves were rattled by news of possible disruptions to supplies in Columbia and Brazil.
A strike by Colombian truck drivers was set to begin at midnight Saturday and looked certain to deepen near-term supply concerns.
But after the London market had closed, a Colombian government minister said the authorities might outlaw the stoppage.

"The strike has all the characteristics of being declared illegal because the government has already complied with 85 percent of the drivers' demands," Transportation Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez said.
In Brazil, stevedores were to present a counter-proposal to private terminal operator Cosipa on Thursday which if accepted may prevent a national strike planned on Friday.
Well-supplied robustas are being weighed by arrivals from the main Indonesian harvest.
Analysts said the technical picture in London could improve if May clears above $1,668, the April 2 high. But it could struggle to regain a foothold at the recent peak of just above $1,800.
